text.p: -- Gruntal analyst David Saks said he raised his rating on Bristol-Myers Squibb Co's shares to outperform from long-term outperform.
-- He raised his 1996 earnings per share forecast for the company to $5.67 from $5.65 and his 1997 EPS view by $0.20 to $6.20. He also set a 1998 EPS forecast of $6.80.

-- He said in a research note that Bristol-Myers was undervalued and that he expected "the high-quality shares to appreciate in response to stronger-than-expected earnings in the upcoming third (quarter), (a) probable dividend hike and (a) likely stock split (2-for-1)."
-- The shares were up 1-7/8 at 96-1/4 at 1300 EDT/1700 GMT Monday.
